text.p: Egypt was the big winner when the curtain was lowered on the eighth Pan-Arab games on Sunday after two weeks of competition.
With 97 golds, 57 silvers and 40 bronzes, Egypt ended the games well ahead of its closest rival, Algeria, which won 43, 44 and 44 respectively.
The flag of the games was handed over to a representative of Jordan, which will host the next games in 2001. Jordan won the soccer final against Syria 1-0 earlier in the evening.
The games were tainted by doping which led to the disqualification of 12 athletes -- five Egyptians two Saudis, two Syrians, an Algerian, a Tunisian and one Kuwaiti.
It was the first time athletes have been disqualified for drug use since the inaugural Games in Alexandria, Egypt in 1953.
The games had a controversial start when hosting Lebanon, under pressure from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, barred 97 Iraqi athletes from competing.
They were stranded at the Syrian-Lebanese border without visas for two days before heading home.
Nearly 2,200 athletes from 19 countries took part in 20 sports.
